# Near-quantile normals and the primary-neutral boundary response

This note quantitatively resolves the deficient-active-normal example
in `candidate 29c345ef7c2b94ab`.
Three exact near-active quantile caps recover the missing vertical
energy normal with multipliers of order 1/beta and aggregate slack of
order beta. It also distinguishes their unrestricted divergent boundary
response from the finite response on a specified primary-neutral action
face. No actual neutral path, critical cover continuation, or secondary
descent is inferred from the latter finite limit.

## 1. The actual frustum and its exact nearby quantiles

Let

    T=conv{v_1=(2,-1), v_2=(-1,2), v_3=(-1,-1)},
    K={ (X,t): -1<=t<=1, X in (1+epsilon t)T },
    0<epsilon<=10^(-9),
    t_0=epsilon/3, A=1+epsilon^2/3, Y=(0,t_0).

The cited all-normal theorem proves that Y is the UNIQUE ordinary
deepest point, the normalized depth is gamma=4/9, and its ONLY oriented
active normals are positive multiples of

    n_1=(1,0), n_2=(0,1), n_3=(-1,-1)

with zero vertical component. The ordinary projective normalizer and
energy gradient at Y are positive vertical vectors. In particular a
secondary energy maximum at this deepest singleton has a nonzero
normal missing from the active cone.

The original volume and raw depth are

    V=|K|=9A,                    Q=gamma V=4A.           (1)

For beta near zero put N_i(beta)=(n_i,beta) and consider

    H_i(beta,c)={N_i(beta).((X,t)-Y)>=c}.

All horizontal slices have the same isolated-vertex status for
|beta|<=1/8 and the small thresholds below. Writing r=1+epsilon t,
q=t-t_0, similarity of the actual triangular slices gives

    |K intersect H_i(beta,c)|
      =(1/2) integral_(-1)^1 (2r+beta q-c)^2 dt
      =Q+(A/3)beta^2-(4-2beta t_0)c+c^2.              (2)

There is no index dependence. The small Q-quantile root is

    c_beta=2-beta t_0-sqrt(4-4beta t_0-beta^2/3)
      = (A beta^2/3)/
          [2-beta t_0+sqrt(4-4beta t_0-beta^2/3)].       (3)

It is positive for beta!=0 and c_0=0. Uniformly for epsilon<=1/2 and
|beta|<=1/8, the denominator in the second expression exceeds 3,
so c_beta<=13 beta^2/108<beta^2/8. Thus
|c_beta-beta(t-t_0)|<1/2<=r on every slice; the cut lies strictly
between the lower and upper vertex heights. This verifies the status
used in (2), rather than merely solving a polynomial outside its
geometric range.

The tail decreases strictly with c in this range, and the proper
section remains positive, so (3) is the actual upper Q quantile. Its
expansion and actual coarea are

    c_beta=(A/12)beta^2+O(beta^3),
    S_beta=-partial_c |K intersect H_i(beta,c)| at c=c_beta
      =4-2beta t_0-2c_beta
      =2sqrt(4-4beta t_0-beta^2/3).                     (4)

These are the displayed, UNNORMALIZED normals. Dividing a normal and
its threshold by its Euclidean length rescales the coarea accordingly;
the geometric cap and every conclusion below are unchanged.

## 2. Exact recovery, two signs, and the necessary multiplier rate

Every point Y+h with depth at least Q satisfies every actual quantile
inequality

                     N_i(beta).h<=c_beta.              (5)

Since sum_i n_i=0, averaging (5) gives beta h_t<=c_beta.
For beta>0 this bounds h_t above by c_beta/beta; for beta<0 it bounds
h_t below by c_beta/beta. Both bounds tend to zero. The active
horizontal inequalities then force h_X=0. This reproduces the
singleton constraint through actual quantiles, rather than replacing
it by a false finite active-normal representation.

For any prescribed g>0 and beta>0, take

    lambda_i(beta)=g/(3beta).

Then there is the EXACT vector identity and vanishing aggregate slack

    sum_i lambda_i N_i(beta)=g e_t,
    sum_i lambda_i c_beta=g c_beta/beta
                       =(gA/12)beta+O(beta^2).         (6)

Negative beta analogously recovers a negative vertical vector using
positive coefficients. In particular (6) recovers the actual positive
energy gradient, or the projective parameter, by choosing its scalar
g. No formula for the numerical value of that projective minimizer is
needed.

For unit normals U_i=N_i/|N_i| the coefficients are instead
g|N_i|/(3beta). Their sum is

    (g/(3beta))[2sqrt(1+beta^2)+sqrt(2+beta^2)],         (7)

while the aggregate slack is still exactly (6). The order 1/|beta| is
necessary, not an artifact of this certificate: a positive conic
combination of unit normals whose vertical components have magnitude
at most eta and whose vertical sum is g must have total coefficient
at least |g|/eta. Here eta is of order |beta|, and (7) attains that
order. The slack itself is quadratic, so the aggregated slack is
linear in |beta|. There is no 1/beta^2 multiplier requirement for this
normal recovery.

The unshifted through-Y caps have raw excess (A/3)beta^2 by (2).
Their coefficient-weighted excess is gA beta/3. This is a different
quantity from the quantile slack in (6); its leading ratio to that
slack is the actual critical coarea S_0=4.

## 3. Relation to the exact quadratic depth loss

At the shifted axis point Y+h e_t, a cap with normal N_i(beta) passes
through that point when c=beta h. Equation (2) becomes

    |K intersect H_i(beta,beta h)|
      =Q-4beta h+beta^2 B(h),
    B(h)=1/3+(t_0+h)^2.                                (8)

Its minimizing tilt is beta_*(h)=2h/B(h), and its minimized raw mass is

                         Q-4h^2/B(h).                 (9)

For the explicit small source neighborhood in the cited frustum
theorem, the all-normal exterior gap proves that this is the ACTUAL
depth, not merely an upper bound from a few caps. Dividing by V=9A
gives its formula. In particular the raw quadratic deficit is

                         (12/A)h^2+o(h^2).             (10)

Thus the zero first-order vertical source constraint is enforced at
second order. Equations (3), (6), and (8) describe the same mechanism:
quantile slack is quadratic in the tilt, source displacement couples
linearly to the tilt, and normal recovery requires reciprocal tilt
multipliers.

## 4. A conditional general near-quantile lemma

Here is the precise part that extends beyond the frustum. Work at an
interior own-fiber source Y=(p,y), with raw depth Q. Take a finite
regular critical circuit with displayed continuous normals u_j and
positive coefficients rho_j satisfying sum rho_j u_j=0. Permit actual
base-normal components as well. For each j choose a LINEAR normal
perturbation whose continuous part is u_j+s w_j, and write its actual
cap mass at threshold c relative to Y as M_j(s,c).

Assume M_j is C2 in a neighborhood of (0,0), its own section is proper,
and

    M_j(0,0)=Q,
    partial_c M_j(0,0)=-S_j<0,
    partial_s M_j(0,0)=0,
    partial_ss M_j(0,0)=A_j.                            (11)

The zero first derivative follows from genuine criticality whenever
this normal perturbation has a two-sided differentiable cap mass:
all the through-Y caps have mass at least Q. The same fact gives
A_j>=0. The C2 hypothesis is additional, not a consequence of an
arbitrary convex body having a regular section. A concrete sufficient
case is a finite family of polytopal fibers with each varying cut
avoiding their vertices and retaining proper/strict-full/strict-empty
statuses in the neighborhood; the actual cap vertices then depend
smoothly on the parameters in a fixed clipping triangulation.

The implicit-function theorem applied ONLY to the scalar threshold
gives actual quantiles

    c_j(0)=c'_j(0)=0,
    c_j(s)=[A_j/(2S_j)]s^2+o(s^2).                   (12)

There is no Slater assumption on the depth region. Set
w=sum rho_j w_j. For s>0, the positive coefficients rho_j/s satisfy

    sum_j (rho_j/s)(u_j+s w_j)=w,
    sum_j (rho_j/s)c_j(s)
       =(s/2)sum_j rho_j A_j/S_j+o(s).               (13)

This is a quantitative latent-normal certificate with actual caps.
It is not an exact-active KKT formula. If all vertical/missing
components are O(s) and w has a nonzero such component, the same
projection argument as in Section 2 forces coefficient growth
Omega(1/s).

The section data in (11) have a useful geometric interpretation. Put
m_j(W)=N_j(0).(W-Y), ell_j(W)=N'_j.(W-Y). With the actual coarea
factor, let J_j(c) be the section integral of ell_j^2 at m_j=c.
Whenever these moments can be differentiated by the local coarea
calculation (in particular in the stable polytopal case above),

    partial_s M_j(0,0)=integral_(m_j=0) ell_j d sigma,
    A_j=-J'_j(0).                                    (14)

The first is the full mixed section-centroid condition. The second
follows by differentiating the slice identity: the second normal
derivative is the derivative of the level delta function, whereas
threshold differentiation has the opposite sign. This can also be
obtained by repeated one-dimensional integration in the fixed clipping
cells; it is not an assumption of a global smooth boundary.

If e is a missing source direction with u_j.e=0 and
d_j=w_j.e!=0 for some j with A_j>0, moving the source by h e changes
that cap threshold to s h d_j. Choosing
s=(S_j d_j/A_j)h in its two-sided parameter neighborhood gives

    depth(Y+h e)<=Q-[S_j^2 d_j^2/(2A_j)]h^2+o(h^2).   (15)

This is only an upper bound on depth; equality requires additional
all-normal control, supplied for the frustum by its separate theorem.
If A_j=0, no quadratic-rate conclusion is drawn from (15). Merely
C1 cap maps still give c_j(s)=o(s) and a limiting certificate under
the analogous hypotheses, but not the quadratic constants above.

## 5. Why scalar boundary responses do not cancel automatically

Let v>=0 be an actual inward first boundary speed on the frustum.
Put

    D=integral_(boundary K) v dS,
    L_i(beta)=integral_(boundary K intersect H_i(beta,c_beta)) v dS,
    R_beta=(1/3)sum_i L_i(beta)-gamma D.                (16)

The caps are proper and have no coincident body facets, so the fixed
closed-cap loss uses these indicators up to surface-null sets. The
normal certificate (6) weights the normalized response by

                   (g/beta) R_beta.                  (17)

Horizontal cancellation of the NORMALS does not imply R_0=0.
If R_0 is nonzero and L_i(beta) is continuous at zero, (17) diverges
with leading term g R_0/beta.

Here is an explicit actual deformation with a nonzero leading term.
Intersect K with

                         t+e |X|^2<=1.

This is a nested convex-body deformation. Its first speed is |X|^2
on the top triangular facet and zero on the other facet interiors;
intersections with their edges have zero surface measure. Set
r_+=1+epsilon. Direct triangle moments give

    integral_T |X|^2 dX=9/2,
    (1/3)sum_i integral_(T intersect {n_i.X>=0}) |X|^2 dX=16/9.

For example each canonical cap is (2/3)T+v_i/3, its centroid is v_i/3,
and average_i |v_i|^2=4, which gives the second identity. Scaling the
top facet therefore yields

    D=(9/2)r_+^4,
    R_0=-(2/9)r_+^4<0.                               (18)

Thus (17) tends to minus infinity as beta decreases to zero. This
example rules out unrestricted use of the recovered energy normal
as a finite boundary stress. It does NOT rule out renormalization on
the primary-neutral face R_0(v)=0. The frustum is a safe body, not a
hypothetical bad shape minimum, and (18) is not a claim that such a
bad minimum admits this nonneutral action.

## 6. The exact primary-neutral angular response

Assume now that v is bounded and continuous on each closed facet of
the frustum, allowing different traces from adjacent facets. Finite
global-cut speeds satisfy this condition on this polytope when their
restrictions to each old facet are continuous; the condition is stated
explicitly rather than asserted for arbitrary measurable speeds.

Let Gamma_i=boundary K intersect {n_i.X=0}. On each facet F crossed by
this plane, let nu_F be its unit normal and

    a_iF=|n_i-(n_i.nu_F)nu_F|>0,

where n_i is embedded horizontally in R3. Every crossing is transverse
on the facet. The finitely many crossings of facet edges have H1
measure zero; no cut plane contains a body edge or facet. Facewise
coarea and continuity give

    L'_i(0)=sum_F integral_(Gamma_i intersect relint F)
                      v(X,t)(t-t_0)/a_iF dH1.         (19)

The threshold term c'_0 is zero by (4). Formula (19) is the angular
derivative of the PRIMARY fixed-cap boundary loss; it is not a new
volume variation identity. Supporting coincidences would require
different one-sided branches and are not covered by (19).

On the specified primary-neutral face R_0(v)=0, equation (17) has the
finite limit

    lim_(beta->0+) (g/beta)R_beta
       =(g/3)sum_i sum_F integral_(Gamma_i intersect relint F)
                      v(X,t)(t-t_0)/a_iF dH1.         (20)

No forbidden signed subtraction is needed: the divergent constant
term is zero by the PREMISE R_0(v)=0. Without that premise the
subtraction would change the nonnegative multiplier problem, as (18)
demonstrates. For bounded measurable v without suitable traces the
derivative in (19) need not exist, so neither (19) nor (20) is then
asserted.

## 7. The remaining source/normal motion term

The actual coarea first moment of the near-quantile section is also
explicit. Let

    M_i(beta)=integral_(boundary H_i(beta,c_beta) intersect K)
                        ((X,t)-Y) dH2/|N_i(beta)|.

Direct section integration gives

    M_i(beta)=(-2c_beta v_i,
                       2t_0 c_beta+(2A/3)beta).       (21)

For i=1, solve X_1=c_beta-beta(t-t_0) and integrate X_2 from -r to
r-c_beta+beta(t-t_0); the surface Jacobian cancels |N_i|. The other
two formulas follow by the affine vertex symmetries. Equation (2)
at its quantile root simplifies the horizontal moments to the stated
vector. Thus M_i(0)=0 but M'_i(0)=(2A/3)e_t.

To identify the actual parameter term, prescribe a mark velocity
dot Y=(xi,h) and bounded cap-normal velocities B_i(beta) converging
to B_i(0). Consider the moving caps

    [N_i(beta)+e B_i(beta)].(W-Y-e dot Y)>=c_beta.

For each FIXED beta, their removed cap mass to first order is

    L_i(beta)+S_beta N_i(beta).dot Y-B_i(beta).M_i(beta). (22)

This is the usual body-loss plus threshold-motion minus section-
normal-motion formula, with the actual unnormalized coarea factors.
Since the near sections are proper, no supporting allocation is being
chosen here.

Assuming R_0(v)=0 and the regularity of Section 6, weighting the
normalized responses in (22) by g/(3beta) and then letting beta->0+
gives EXACTLY

    g R'_0 + 4g h - (2gA/9) sum_i B_(i,t)(0).          (23)

The horizontal mark term cancels because sum n_i=0; the horizontal
normal-motion terms vanish because c_beta=O(beta^2). The vertical
source and normal-motion terms in (23) remain. Setting the cap
parameters artificially to zero would discard them, not prove them
irrelevant.

Alternatively, hold normals fixed and retune each quantile threshold
to the moving normalized level gamma |K_e|. Its threshold derivative
is forced by its OWN scalar mass equation:

    dot c_i(beta)=-[L_i(beta)-gamma D]/S_beta.          (24)

With a normal velocity, add B_i.M_i to the numerator with the opposite
sign of the body loss. Such separate retuning cancels that individual
normalized response by definition; it does not show that all thresholds
come from one admissible moving source, or preserve a selected cover.

There is a further incidence issue before any descent argument. For
beta!=0 all three Q-quantile caps exclude Y because c_beta>0, and their
normals sum to 3beta e_t. They are NOT a positive circuit covering its
fiber plane or the whole body. A source shift and/or additional cap
selection must be justified independently. The recovered constrained
normal and the neutral response (20)--(23) therefore provide a real
second-order/lexicographic tangent interface, but not a continuation of
a neutral primary path or a closure of the variational argument.

## 8. An actual neutral path where source motion cancels the finite term

The remaining mark term in (23) can be essential even for a completely
explicit compatible path. Fix 0<a<1/2, so Y+a e_t lies in the interior
of K, and set

    K_e=(1-e)K+e(Y+a e_t).

This is a nested homothety toward an interior point. Its unique deepest
point is Y_e=Y+e a e_t and its normalized depth remains exactly gamma
by affine invariance. The first inward speed is

    v=h_(K-Y)(nu)-a nu_t>0.

Divergence on the proper cap H_i(beta,c_beta), with its actual section
coarea, gives

    integral_(body cap boundary) h_(K-Y)(nu) dS
       =3Q+c_beta S_beta,
    integral_(body cap boundary) nu_t dS=beta S_beta.

The total first loss is D=3V. Consequently

    L_i(beta)-gamma D=(c_beta-a beta)S_beta,
    R_0=0,                    R'_0=-4a.                (25)

Thus the renormalized fixed-cap angular term is NONZERO, namely -4ga.
The genuine deepest-mark velocity has h=a, and its term +4ga in (23)
cancels it exactly. A putative secondary conclusion based on the
angular term alone would discard this actual motion.

If one follows the exact affine images of the quantile caps as well,
their threshold relative to Y_e is (1-e)c_beta. Its additional relative
threshold derivative -c_beta removes the remaining c_beta S_beta in
the finite-beta response, so the full normalized response is exactly
zero before any beta limit. If relative threshold is held fixed as in
(22), that remaining term is O(beta^2) and has zero renormalized limit.
This identifies all terms without postulating an abstract neutral
continuation. It does not say that an arbitrary neutral speed has such
a path or such a moving deepest point.
